title: On-call and Incident Response: Process, Runbooks, Rotations, and Templates
author: Nora Kim
content:
Summary:
This document describes Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes, runbook patterns, postmortem template, rotation policies, game day guidance, and status page / customer comms templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders, and product owners.

Scope:
- Services covered: Redwood API (hosted inference), routing/ingress, runtime scheduler, KV cache, metrics/tracing pipeline, auth & billing systems.
- Audience: on-call engineers, IC/secondary responders, incident commander (ICM), product owners, support & customer success.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection: alert fires (monitoring / synthetic tests / user reports).
2) Triage: primary on-call acknowledges within 5 minutes (SLA).
3) Mitigation: reduce customer impact via rollback, routing shift, throttling, or fallback model.
4) Resolution: root cause identified and fix applied or planned.
5) Post-incident: postmortem written within 72 hours, action items tracked.

Severity classification and initial response targets:
- Sev 1 (P0): system-wide outage, customer-facing downtime, or >50% traffic affected. Acknowledge <1 min, IC assigned <5 min, 24/7 escalation.
- Sev 2 (P1): significant functional degradation (latency or errors) for a large cohort. Acknowledge <5 min, IC assigned <15 min.
- Sev 3 (P2): partial degradation or single-customer impact. Acknowledge <30 min.
- Sev 4 (P3): low-impact bug or internal issue; tracked in backlog.

On-call rota and escalation policy:
- Roles: Primary (first responder), Secondary (backup), Incident Commander (ICM), PagerDuty escalation policy.
- Rotation cadence: 1 week for primary/secondary, handover on Monday 09:00 UTC.
- Shift coverage: Primary + Secondary weekdays 09:00-18:00 local, on-call covers nights and weekends with on-call pay & compensatory time.
- Escalation timeline: primary 0–15 min, escalate to secondary 15–30 min, IC 30–45 min if unresolved.
- Handover checklist (to be posted in #oncall-handover Slack): active incidents, scheduled maintenance, flaky alerts to silence, ongoing mitigations.

Pager thresholds (examples):
- API error rate > 5% sustained for 3 minutes -> Sev 2 alert.
- Token generation latency p95 > 2.5s for 5 minutes -> Sev 2.
- GPU OOM or node offline -> Sev 1 if impacts >2 pods.
- KV cache miss spike leading to >3x cost -> Sev 3.

Runbook patterns (general):
- Goal: make the first 15 minutes of troubleshooting deterministic. Each runbook must contain: symptom, scope-check queries, quick mitigations, authoritative logs/metrics, escalation contacts, and post-incident follow-ups.

Runbook: API high error-rate (example)
- Symptom: 5xx rate increases to >5% of traffic for 3m.
- Scope checks:
  - Grafana: services.api.errors / service:api / 5xx / last 15m
  - SLO dashboard: error budget burn rate
  - Checks: are migrations/deploys occurring? (/concourse or ci pipeline)
- Quick mitigations (in order):
  1) Disable recent canary (if a rollout is ongoing): `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-service --to-revision=<previous>`
  2) Increase error budget-based throttling: toggle `feature.flags.rate_limit_override` -> true
  3) Route traffic to Dedicated fallback model: update routing rule in console or `redwood route set --fallback-model=...`
- Logs & useful queries:
  - `curl -sS https://elk.internal/_search?q=service:api AND status:[500 TO 599]`
  - Trace link pattern: https://traces.redwood-internal/{{trace_id}}
- Escalation: notify #oncall, page secondary, contact owner: @api-team-lead.
- Post-incident: create postmortem, add template items below, and schedule follow-up with API product owner within 3 business days.

Runbook: Inference p95 latency spike
- Symptom: inference p95 > SLO (2.5s) for >5 minutes.
- Quick checks:
  - Check scheduler queue length and GPU utilization (Grafana / K8s metrics).
  - Check KV cache hit rate.
  - Confirm no large batch job started recently.
- Quick mitigation steps:
  1) Reduce max_batch_size for the model in serving config to lower tail latency.
  2) Enable CPU fallback routing for non-critical tenants.
  3) Scale up Dedicated pool if autoscaling is stuck: `terraform apply` or use console scale action.
- Owner contacts: @runtime-team, @infra-oncall.

Runbook: GPU node OOM / eviction
- Symptom: node lost/gpu driver crash, pods evicted, inference jobs failing.
- Steps:
  1) Mark node unschedulable: `kubectl cordon <node>`
  2) Drain non-critical pods: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets`
  3) If driver crash: collect dmesg & driver logs to /tmp/incident-logs and reboot node via cloud provider console.
  4) If broad capacity impact, shift traffic to Dedicated fallback pool and notify Sales for impacted customers.

Communication: internal and external
- Internal incident comms:
  - Use #incident-<id> Slack channel for coordination.
  - Post periodic updates (every 15 min for Sev1, every 60 min for Sev2) with: current impact, mitigation steps, next actions, owner.
  - Create a wartime doc in Confluence (link added to Slack channel) to capture timeline and decisions.
- Status page template (short):
  - Title: [Identified] Degraded inference latency affecting hosted API
  - Impact: Some customers may experience slower responses or transient failures.
  - Affected services: Redwood API, runtime scheduler (region-name).
  - Start time: 2026-02-28T14:35Z
  - Latest update: 2026-02-28T14:50Z - Applying routing change to reduce impact
  - Next update: 2026-02-28T15:05Z or when new information is available
  - Workaround: Use Dedicated/Private endpoints where available; contact support@redwood.ai for SLA-sensitive traffic
- Customer comms templates (email/CS):
  - Subject: Incident update: [Service] degradation on 2026-02-28
  - Body:
    Hello <CustomerName>,

    We are investigating an issue causing intermittent degraded performance for the Redwood API. Our engineers have identified the root cause and are actively applying mitigations. We will provide updates every 30 minutes until resolved.

    Impact: <brief description>
    ETA for full resolution: <if available>
    Temporary workaround: <if available>

    If you are seeing production impact that requires immediate attention, please reply to this email and our support team will prioritize your account.

    Sincerely,
    Redwood Inference Support

Postmortem template (required for Sev1 & Sev2 within 72 hours):
- Title: [SEV#] Short descriptive title
- Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-###
- Timeline: ordered timestamps (UTC) with actor and step
- Impact: customers affected, SLOs breached, business impact estimate
- Root cause: succinct explanation
- Contributing factors: systemic or process items
- Immediate remediation: what fixed it in the short term
- Long-term fix & owner: action items with owner and ETA (track as JIRA tickets)
- Lessons learned & action plan for preventing recurrence
- Postmortem review date & attendees

Game days and preparedness:
- Quarterly game days run by eng-sre to validate runbooks, on-call handovers, and blast-radius minimization.
- Example scenarios: full regional outage, unexpectedly slow model, drain/evict node test, status page update practice.
- Outcomes: action items tracked publicly, runbook updates scheduled, and on-call training for new hires.

SLOs and error budgets (examples):
- API availability: 99.95% monthly (measured by successful request rate).
- Generation latency: p95 < 2.5s for hosted tiers.
- Errors: 5xx < 0.5% monthly.
- When an SLO is at risk (burn rate > 5x), create a high-priority incident and engage product/operator leads.

Ownership & contacts (primary):
- On-call: see PagerDuty schedule (link in Confluence ticket).
- Incident Commander rota: eng-sre leads, contact via #eng-sre on Slack.
- Customer comms: customer-success@redwood.ai and assigned AE.

Maintenance & noisy alert hygiene:
- Weekly review of top 20 alerts by noise and actionability. Silence or lower severity for known non-actionable alerts.
- If an alert is silenced for >72 hours, document reasoning in the alert definition page.

Metrics and evidence to capture during incidents:
- Request rates, error rates (5xx), latencies (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, scheduler queue length, KV cache hit/miss, recent deploys.
- Always attach relevant graphs to the incident Slack channel and wartime doc.

Appendix: useful commands & links
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/ops
- Tracing: https://traces.redwood-internal/
- Log search: https://elk.redwood-internal/
- PagerDuty: https://adpd.pagerduty.com/schedules/Redwood-Oncall

Document maintenance:
- Owners must review this document at least annually or after any Sev1 incident.
- Changes should be submitted as PRs to Confluence with reviewers from eng-sre and runtime teams.
